title: Stateful Large Language Model Serving with Pensieve
technique: stateful multi-turn serving: two-tier (GPU+CPU) KV cache of conversation history with eviction/swap scheduling, plus a generalized PagedAttention kernel for multi-token queries over non-contiguous cache

optimized_metrics.evidence: Pensieve is designed to optimize both peak throughput and latency of serving LLM in conversational scenarios.
Pensieve is designed to optimize both peak throughput and latency of serving LLM in conversational scenarios. ... we measure the achieved serving throughput and 90-percentile normalized latency
optimized_metrics.locator: §6.1 Performance Metric (but see extractor_notes: §6.2 says mean)
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: The normalized latency is calculated as the mean of each request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length (§6.2); contrast §6.1: "90-percentile normalized latency"

headline_claim.text: Pensieve can achieve 1.14-3.0x the throughput of vLLM and TensorRT-LLM and significantly reduce latency.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 10-13 (req/s at a fixed per-token latency target, e.g. 120 ms/token)
avg tokens processed in prefill (recomputation avoided), §6.2

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we measure the achieved serving throughput and 90-percentile normalized latency, which is calculated as the end-to-end request serving latency divided by the number of output tokens.
The normalized latency is calculated as the mean of each request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length, as done in [27, 52].
metric_definitions.notes: States mean here; internal inconsistency with §6.1 (P90 vs mean). Output length only in denominator.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Pensieve's throughput is 1.36x of vLLM and 1.14x of TensorRT-LLM for serving OPT-13B at 120 ms per token latency, and 1.70x of vLLM and 1.58x of TensorRT-LLM for serving Llama 2-13B at 180 ms per token latency.
metric_definitions.notes: Throughput in req/s read off the normalized-latency vs throughput curve at a chosen per-token latency target (100-400 ms/token, picked per model/dataset); requests are conversation turns.

slo_spec: No formal SLO; comparison at a per-model normalized-latency level (OPT-13B 120 ms/token, Llama2-13B 100-180 ms/token, Llama2-70B 400 ms/token).
load_regime: request-rate sweep; conversations arrive Poisson, simulated user think time between turns; ShareGPT and UltraChat
tradeoff_acknowledged: Swap/transfer overheads and GPU-cache contention under high rates (GPU-only cache variant loses gain); CPU cache transfer 18-20% throughput drop when swapping in both directions without optimization.
hardware: Azure NC A100 v4, up to 4x A100-80GB, 24-core EPYC, 220 GB RAM
models: OPT-13B, Llama 2-13B (1 GPU); OPT-66B, Llama 2-70B (4 GPUs)
workloads: ShareGPT, UltraChat multi-turn conversation traces with Poisson arrivals and think time
extractor_notes: The metric paragraph (§6.1) says 90-percentile normalized latency but §6.2 and the figures define it as the MEAN of per-request E2E/output length (copied from vLLM). The stat is recorded as mean; flag as ambiguous. Latency/throughput are per conversation turn request, with history length counted only in prefill.
load_class_quote: we simulate a request's arrival time by sampling from a Poisson distribution under different request rates (§6.1)
repass_log: THR_REQ, NORM_LAT: design ('Pensieve is designed to optimize both peak throughput and latency')
NORM_LAT stat: explicit but internally inconsistent in paper (§6.1 '90-percentile' vs §6.2 'mean'); kept mean per §6.2/Fig 10 definition, conflict noted in stat_quote
